loose_hits_inspected.title: A Square-Root Obstruction to The K = 4 Phylogenetic-Network Enumeration Conjecture
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Batle conjectured that, for fixed reticulation number k, the difference between the numbers of reticulation-visible and tree-child networks is a sum of two prescribed factorial bases with polynomial coefficients. We disprove the conjecture at its first open case, k = 4. If X = (1-2z) 1/2 and R4(z) is the exponential generating function for reticulation-visible networks, the Chang-Fuchs component-graph formula gives [X 3 ]R4(z) = 5/16. A highest-exponent argument isolates this coefficient in the unique four-sink component graph, so the disproof does not depend on a large numerical enumeration. Neither proposed factorial basis can produce a positive odd power X j with j > 1. We also compute the corrected exact formula: it contains the additional term 15(2ℓ-5)!!/16. Two independent exact implementations certify the full Laurent generating function and an integer residual against the conjectured degree bounds.

loose_hits_inspected.title: Closing the Permanent-Rank Boundary for the Alon–Jaeger–Tarsi Conjecture
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Let \( p\geq 5 \) be prime. The theorem of Yu obtained from permanent rank proves the Alon--Jaeger--Tarsi conjecture over \( F_p \) in dimensions \( n<2^{p-2} \). We close the missing boundary: the conjecture holds for every \( n\leq 2^{p-2} \). In particular, for every \( M\in GL_8(F_5) \) there is a vector \( x\in(F_5^*)^8 \) such that \( Mx\in(F_5^*)^8 \). The proof separates according to the permanent rank of \( M \). Above half rank, Yu's concatenation recurrence and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz force a nowhere-zero point. At equality, the rigidity theorem of Kisley and Shader reduces \( M \), under monomial equivalence, to a direct sum of \( 2\times2 \) blocks, for which a nowhere-zero point is explicit.

loose_hits_inspected.title: Links-Gould Positivity for Two-Block Alternating 2-Bridge Knots
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Ishii conjectured that the coefficients of the Links-Gould polynomial of an alternating knot have signs determined, up to one global sign, by total degree parity. We prove the positive normalization of this conjecture for the two-block alternating 2-bridge knots D(p, q), with p, q ≥ 1, in Kohli's notation. More precisely, we give an explicit factorization of LG(D(p, q);-x,-y) as a sum of products of Laurent polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. The proof is symbolic and uses Kohli's three-term skein recurrence; exact computations serve only as independent checks. The result does not assert hole-freeness or log-concavity, and the conjecture for arbitrary alternating knots remains open.

loose_hits_inspected.title: Uniform Block-Projection and Matching Bounds in a Frankl Three-Cover Branch
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: We derive uniform and exact restrictions inside the full three-cover branch of the current structure theory for a smallest emptyset-free height-five counterexample to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture. Write r for the number of nonprivate coordinates and t = 2r+5+s, where s ≥ 0. If q0 is the size of the fiber with empty private support and q2 counts residual members with two private coordinates, we prove the independent bounds q0 + q2 ≥ 2, q0 ≤ ⌈(2r + s)/3⌉-1. The main tool is a ground-independent block-projection inequality. A height-two fiber produces disjoint complement blocks, and projection closure forces a concave incidence cost in every other fiber. At the specific point (r, s) = (10, 2), a sharper integer recurrence proves q0 ≤ 4; its seven excluded values have minimum gaps 10, 39, 67, 86, 113, 129, 153. Independent exact implementations audit the analytic reductions, the fixed-point recurrence, and the finite case split underlying the low-end bound. These are strict partial structural results: they neither eliminate the full three-cover branch nor settle the height-five case.

loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Let p n be the nth prime and let a 0 = 0, with a n equal to the largest odd divisor of a n-1 + p n. The OEIS entry A114216 asks whether a 33900 = 1 is the last occurrence of 1. We give the exact counterexample n = 78,493,252. At this index, p n = 1,579,691,809 and a n-1 = 567,791,839, whose sum is 2 31. Two independent exact-integer implementations reconstruct the prime index and the recurrence state.

loose_hits_inspected.title: The Distinct-Cycle-Length Probability is Strictly Decreasing after 30
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Let qn be the probability that the cycle lengths of a uniformly random permutation in Sn are pairwise distinct. We prove qn+1 < qn for every n ≥ 30. The proof factors the difference generating function (1-z) k≥1 (1 + z k /k) as W (z 2)J(z). An elementary recurrence gives a uniform coefficient estimate for W , while absolute moment and pointwise bounds for J preserve a parity cancellation at z =-1. Explicit constants make every difference negative from degree 5000 onward. The remaining finite comparisons are certified by exact integer arithmetic and independently by outward-rounded rational intervals.

loose_hits_inspected.title: Finite‑prime obstructions for Erdős Problem 1212
loose_hits_inspected.abstract: Erdős asked whether the visible lattice graph contains a path to infinity through points whose coordinates exceed 1 and are not both prime. The question remains open. We prove a necessary condition for any such path. For an integer \(M \ge 2\), consider the periodic set of pairs for which no prime divisor of M divides both coordinates, while some prime divisor of M divides at least one coordinate. Every unit‑neighbour component of this set is finite. With \(R=\mathrm{rad}(M)\), we classify components by the R-grid and give an explicit bound obtained from an exact Chinese remainder count. It follows that every hypothetical solution path encounters simultaneously B-rough coordinates at uniformly bounded path‑index gaps. Combining this recurrence with the factorial‑wall drift obstruction shows that such simultaneous roughness occurs arbitrarily far from the diagonal.
